lines.text: Ski season is here, but the snow on many slopes didn't fall from the sky. It came out of a cannon.
Snow guns spray a fine mist of water into cold air, with a big fan or compressed air flinging it high over the trail.
As some droplets evaporate, they pull heat out of the air, cooling it enough to freeze the droplets around them.
Some machines also add nucleating agents, which help the droplets freeze faster.
Humidity matters as much as temperature. Crews watch the wet bulb temperature, and in very dry air they can even make snow a bit above freezing.
Machine snow is denser and rounder, because each droplet gets only a short drop to freeze, not a long fall from a cloud.
